seal.statement: Starting from the independently verified phases-1-through-5 raft-rs integration at fe6e04c3d, replace the rejected public Raft/node/control object boundary with an operation-only partition port. Callers may invoke measured semantic operations and read immutable snapshots by value, but cannot obtain or traverse a RawNode, raft-rs facade, handle, runtime host, group object, lifecycle decision input, durable lifecycle record, SQLite connection, mutable lifecycle state, or provider control. One private runtime owner is the sole production importer and invoker of the raft-rs binding; every actual core entry is counted at that lowest common invocation boundary and follows the private durable lifecycle eligibility owner. One lifecycle owner is the sole production writer of durable replica retirement, lifecycle administration is a separate command surface, and partitionControlOf or any replacement control accessor is absent. Logical retirement, group/runtime health, and host-operation failure remain independent; provenance is constructed as host preparation, private core result, then host persistence/send/apply. A host failure during an in-progress Ready cycle marks only that group recovery-required, and no subsequent operation enters its stale RawNode before reconstruction from coherent durable state. Persistence, send, address-resolution, and application failures each prove reconstruction under the same logical replica and peer identity without retirement or shared-runtime poisoning; a genuine core fatal likewise preserves logical identity across runtime reconstruction. Retirement remains terminal across restart even when stale ConfState contains self: every public active operation refuses before core entry, the core-entry count stays zero, no messages or term disturbance occur, and a deliberate lifecycle-owner bypass restores the old disruptive behavior. The real SQLite transaction boundary proves application effects and durable applied progress cannot split. A mechanical before/after inventory must show that the redesign removes more public capability than it adds, and transport remains blocked until an independent verifier approves the structural boundary.
